summary: Surface Pro (ARM) dual-radio metric flip during roam causes WireGuard split-tunnel to lose internal routes
description:
Issue summary: Multiple Surface Pro (ARM) devices reporting sudden loss of access to internal services immediately after roaming between 2.4GHz and 5GHz SSIDs. VPN (WireGuard) remains 'connected' but traffic to internal subnets (10.10.0.0/16) no longer flows. Impact: several engineers working on private repos and internal dashboards were blocked. Scope: 6 confirmed machines in SF office, same Wi-Fi AP cluster, mixed OS build 22H2 on ARM.

Expected behaviour: roam completes, VPN stays connected and internal routes remain pinned via split-tunnel rules.

Observed behaviour: after roam, Windows chooses different physical adapter and flips interface metrics; WireGuard continues with handshake but system route table places default for internal subnets via physical adapter that has no corporate VLAN reachability, causing traffic to leave on guest VLAN and be dropped by edge firewall.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start WireGuard client connected to corporate split-tunnel config (internal subnets pinned).
2) On Surface Pro ARM device, trigger 2.4GHz->5GHz roam (walk between APs or toggle radio to force handoff).
3) Observe Windows network interface metric and route table immediately after roam (use `Get-NetIPInterface` / `route print`).
4) Attempt to reach internal service (e.g., git.redwood.internal:22 or 10.10.5.12) — connect fails despite WireGuard reported as connected.
5) Compare traffic path with packet capture on client (Wireshark) and AP logs.
6) Reboot or manually set interface metric back and confirm connectivity returns.
logs:
Selected excerpts: 
- WireGuard status: peer=corp-peer latest-handshake=0s transfer=12.4 MiB/1.2 MiB
- Windows Event Log (NetworkProfile) 2026-02-24 09:18:12: Interface metric changed: InterfaceIndex=23 old=25 new=2
- netsh interface ip show config (post-roam): Ethernet 23 (Wi-Fi-5G): Metric 2, IPv4 DHCP, DNS suffix not set
- route print (post-roam): 10.10.0.0 mask 255.255.0.0 192.168.50.1 if 23 metric 2
- AP Controller logs: client A: roam success to AP-B bssid=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, assigned VLAN guest (300) due to NDP mismatch
investigation_notes: 2026-02-24 09:40 - Triage: Confirmed 3 devices reproducing sequence in SF office. WireGuard shows active encryption, but system route points to wrong gateway (guest VLAN). Hypothesis: driver or Windows automatic metric change after roam causing routes to prefer a non-corporate interface.

2026-02-24 11:15 - Network Eng (Diego): AP controller performed VLAN reassignment for those client sessions on roam due to sticky client policy; observed DHCP lease refresh mapping client to guest VLAN for short window (30s) before corporate VLAN restored.

2026-02-24 14:05 - Windows sysadmin (Liam): Verified Windows behavior: on ARM build 22H2 with specific Qualcomm driver v4.2.0.13, `Automatic metric` flag toggles on roam, recalculating interface metric and reordering route table. Confirmed that persistent split-tunnel routes remain but traffic egresses via interface with lower metric to non-corporate gateway.

2026-02-25 09:12 - Repro test: Disabled 'EnableReassociation' on AP and forced roam — metric flip still occurs but VLAN remains corporate; suggests dual contribution: both AP transient VLAN assignment and client metric recalculation necessary to cause outage.

2026-02-26 10:00 - Vendor engagement: Opened ticket with Qualcomm driver team; they acknowledged a known issue where NDIS 6.70 events trigger metric recalculation on 802.11r handoff for certain NIC firmware. Vendor provided a beta driver that pins interface metric.
2026-02-27 16:30 - Mitigation test: Applied local Group Policy (script) to set interface metrics to higher priority for corporate SSID; confirmed successful mitigation on 5 test devices.

2026-03-01 08:00 - Rollout: Deployed updated WireGuard client (1.2.3) which ignores ephemeral route replacements for pinned subnets, and pushed GPO to fleet to set explicit interface metrics for corporate SSIDs. Monitoring shows no recurrences in SF cluster after change.
comments: Asha Patel (2026-02-24 09:25): Reported by eng team after losing access to internal dashboards post-meeting roam. Attached Wireshark capture and `route print`.
Support - Liam O'Connor (2026-02-24 09:35): Acknowledged, investigating. Asking for affected device model list and timestamps.
Network - Diego Ramos (2026-02-24 11:20): Looked into AP controller logs; saw transient VLAN assignment during reassoc. Noted sticky-client policy triggered on AP-B.
QA - Mei Chen (2026-02-25 10:10): Reproduced with debug build; metric flips observed only on Qualcomm NICs on ARM Surface. Intel x86 devices unaffected.
Qualcomm Vendor Rep (2026-02-26 13:04): Confirmed similar reports; provided driver beta and will include long-term fix in upcoming firmware.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-27 17:00): Deployed GPO with interface metric script to 200-device pilot (SF office + remote ARM devices). Please validate if anyone still sees issue.
Asha Patel (2026-03-01 08:12): Confirmed fixed for previously impacted machines. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
resolution:
Root cause: Interaction between AP controller transient VLAN reassignment during roam and Qualcomm Wi-Fi NDIS driver behavior on ARM devices that triggers automatic interface metric recalculation. This allowed split-tunnel routes to be overshadowed by a lower-metric gateway on the guest VLAN.

Immediate remediation: 1) Deployed a client-side mitigation: Group Policy to set explicit interface metric for corporate SSID and a PowerShell script to re-assert routes for 10.10.0.0/16 on network change. 2) Updated WireGuard client to 1.2.3 which rejects ephemeral route replacements for pinned subnets. 3) Adjusted AP controller sticky-client policy to avoid transient VLAN flips during 802.11r handoffs on the affected AP cluster.

Permanent fix / follow-up: Qualcomm to release driver firmware with NDIS fix (vendor ticket QC-29812). IT will monitor and schedule driver rollout after vendor QA. Created follow-up internal task INT-356802 to track vendor driver validation and fleet upgrade.
